q: A purchase order is placed on F.O.R. despatch station terms for stores to be despatched from the supplier's station. Under such terms, the freight for carriage of the consignment to the destination is borne by:

options.A: The supplier, F.O.R. terms always including freight to destination
options.B: The Railway as consignee, the contract price covering the cost of the stores put on rail at the despatch station
options.D: The inspecting agency which inspected the stores

e: FOR despatch station terms mean the price covers the stores put on rail at the despatch station. Freight from that station to destination is therefore borne by the Railway as consignee.

q: Stores are ordered on F.O.R. destination terms. Until the stores are delivered at the destination named in the contract, the risk of loss or damage to the stores in transit rests with:

options.A: The consignee depot, from the moment of despatch by the supplier
options.B: The stock verifier of the destination depot
options.D: The supplier, the price being payable for stores delivered at the destination

e: Under FOR destination terms the price is payable for stores delivered at the named destination, so the risk of loss or damage in transit remains with the supplier until delivery there.

q: A wagon load of stores reaches a depot with its seals found broken and the contents suspected to be disturbed. To protect the Railway's claim for any shortage or damage found, the consignment is correctly taken over by:

options.A: Accepting the consignment without any remark on its condition
options.B: Refusing to unload the wagon in all cases
options.C: Taking open delivery, the contents being checked and the condition and shortage, if any, recorded at the time of delivery in the presence of the competent railway staff
options.D: Taking the full booked quantity into stock irrespective of the quantity found

e: A wagon received with broken seals and suspected disturbance is taken on open delivery: contents are checked and the condition and any shortage recorded at delivery before competent staff, protecting the Railway's claim.

q: The Price Ledger number of a stores item in the unified Priced Vocabulary is allotted by:

options.A: The competent authority maintaining the unified vocabulary of stores, and not by an individual depot storekeeper for his own depot
options.B: Each depot storekeeper independently for the items stocked by him
options.C: The supplier supplying the item to the Railways
options.D: The stock verifier at the time of stock verification

e: PL numbers in the unified Priced Vocabulary are allotted by the competent authority maintaining that vocabulary, ensuring one number and one nomenclature per item across all depots.

q: Rejected stores continue to lie at the consignee depot and the supplier does not remove them within the period allowed, despite notice given to him under the contract. After such notice, the Railway may correctly:

options.A: Issue the rejected stores to departments as serviceable stores
options.B: Appropriate the rejected stores free of cost in all cases without any notice
options.C: Recover the value of the rejected stores from the depot storekeeper
options.D: Deal with the stores as provided in the contract at the cost and risk of the supplier, such as returning or disposing of them and recovering the expenses incurred from the supplier

e: Rejected stores not removed by the supplier within the allowed period after notice are dealt with as provided in the contract at the supplier's cost and risk, including return or disposal, with expenses recovered from him.

q: Stores required for dealing with emergencies such as floods and breaches on a section, like boulders, sandbags and tools, are stocked for immediate use by:

options.A: Procuring them after the emergency has actually occurred in every case
options.B: Keeping them to a prescribed scale at the nominated depots or locations on the section, ready for immediate despatch when an emergency arises
options.C: Holding them only at the headquarters depot of the railway
options.D: Borrowing them from contractors after the emergency is over

e: Emergency stores like boulders, sandbags and tools are stocked to a prescribed scale at nominated depots or locations on the section, ready for immediate despatch when a flood or breach occurs.

q: Tenderers have submitted samples along with their offers in a stores tender, and the tender has been decided. The samples of the tenderers whose offers have not been accepted are correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Retaining them in the depot permanently without any record
options.B: Selling them as scrap along with the depot's scrap
options.C: Returning them to the tenderers concerned after the tender is decided, the sample of the accepted tenderer being retained as required for comparison with the supplies
options.D: Issuing them to consuming departments as stores

e: After a tender is decided, samples of unsuccessful tenderers are returned to them. Only the accepted tenderer's sample is retained, as required, for comparison with the bulk supplies.

q: A tenderer's offer for stores shows a discrepancy between the unit rate quoted and the total amount worked out in the offer. In evaluating the offer, the discrepancy is ordinarily resolved by:

options.A: Taking the unit rate quoted as governing and correcting the total accordingly, as per the tender conditions
options.B: Rejecting the tenderer's earnest money and debarring him
options.C: Taking whichever figure is higher for the Railway
options.D: Asking the tenderer to submit a fresh tender after the opening

e: Where an offer's unit rate and total disagree, the unit rate quoted ordinarily governs under the tender conditions and the total is corrected accordingly for evaluation.

q: During evaluation of a stores tender, the purchase office seeks a clarification from a tenderer on a point in his offer. Such a clarification is permissible only insofar as it:

options.A: Allows the tenderer to reduce his quoted rate after the opening
options.B: Allows the tenderer to change the specifications of the stores offered
options.C: Substitutes a new offer in place of the original offer
options.D: Explains the offer as submitted, without changing its substance, including its price and the stores offered

e: A post-opening clarification may only explain the offer as submitted. It cannot change its substance - neither the price nor the stores offered - and cannot become a substitute or revised offer.

q: The purchaser of a scrap lot deposits the sale value by a cheque, and the cheque is dishonoured before delivery of the lot is effected. The depot correctly:

options.A: Delivers the lot, the cheque having been accepted once
options.B: Does not allow delivery of the lot and takes action to cancel or deal with the sale under the conditions of sale, the sale value having not been actually realised
options.C: Recovers the amount from the earnest money of the other bidders
options.D: Issues the material to a consuming department against the dishonoured cheque

e: A dishonoured cheque means the sale value is not realised. Delivery of the scrap lot is not allowed and the sale is cancelled or otherwise dealt with under the conditions of sale.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 96 lakh and the total issues during the year are Rs 6 crore. The Turnover Ratio of stores is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance / total issues = Rs 96 lakh / Rs 600 lakh (Rs 6 crore) = 0.16. A lower ratio shows stock is turning over faster against issues.

q: A registered firm has repeatedly supplied stores late and with quality complaints recorded against it. Its performance rating is taken into account by the purchase organisation for:

options.A: Fixing the market price of the stores items it supplies
options.B: Assessing the firm on quality, delivery and service, and guiding its registration and consideration in tenders
options.C: Deciding the promotions of the stores staff dealing with the firm
options.D: Clearing the firm's imported consignments through Customs

e: A registered firm's performance rating assesses it on quality, delivery and service from its past supplies. The purchase organisation uses it to guide the firm's registration and its consideration in future tenders.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 9,000 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 100 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 5 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x annual demand x ordering cost / carrying cost) = square root of (2 x 9,000 x 100 / 5) = square root of 3,60,000 = 600 units.

q: A stores depot has to be placed in the charge of its officer-in-charge for day-to-day custody and working. The officer in charge of a stores depot is the:
e: Day-to-day custody and working of a stores depot rests with its officer-in-charge, the Depot Materials Superintendent (DMS), under the overall control of the Controller of Stores organisation.

q: The AAC of an item is 9,600 units. The stock in hand is 1,000 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 600 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Monthly consumption = AAC / 12 = 9,600 / 12 = 800 units. Coverage = (stock + dues) / monthly consumption = (1,000 + 600) / 800 = 2 months.

q: The Tender Accepting Authority does not agree with the rate recommended by the Stores Tender Committee in a particular case. The correct course for the authority is to:

options.A: Accept the Committee's recommendation in every case, as it is binding on him
options.B: Differ from the recommendation, for reasons to be recorded
options.C: Decide the tender without placing the Committee's recommendation on record
options.D: Accept the tender only if the lowest tenderer agrees with the Committee

e: The Tender Accepting Authority is not bound by the Tender Committee's recommendation. He may differ from it, but only for reasons recorded in writing on the tender file.

q: A depot holds 450 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 40 per unit. A fresh receipt of 150 units is taken into stock at Rs 64 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
e: Revised book rate = (450 x Rs 40 + 150 x Rs 64) / (450 + 150) = (18,000 + 9,600) / 600 = 27,600 / 600 = Rs 46 per unit, the weighted average rate.

q: In the tender documents of a stores tender, the Earnest Money Deposit to be furnished by tenderers is referred to, in the terminology of the General Financial Rules, as:
e: In GFR terminology, the Earnest Money Deposit furnished with a tender is called Bid Security; the deposit after award for due performance is Performance Security.

q: The average consumption of an item is 140 units per week, the lead time is 7 weeks and the safety (buffer) stock is 350 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = (average consumption x lead time) + safety stock = (140 x 7) + 350 = 980 + 350 = 1,330 units.

q: A zonal railway centralises the purchase of an item which its depots had earlier been buying separately in small lots. The principal advantage secured by such centralised purchase is:

options.A: Faster delivery of stores to the depots
options.B: Bulk-buying economies and uniformity of specifications and rates
options.C: Elimination of the need for stock verification

e: Centralised purchase of an item secures bulk-buying economies through larger quantities and ensures uniformity of specifications and rates across depots, instead of fragmented small-lot buying.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 7,00,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 4 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5% of the value of the stores in arrear per week of delay amount to:
e: Liquidated damages = value in arrear x rate per week x weeks late = Rs 7,00,000 x 0.5 per cent x 4 = Rs 7,00,000 x 0.005 x 4 = Rs 14,000, as per the LD clause in GCC for Supply.

q: During stock verification of an item, the stock verifier records the quantity actually found in the depot on physical verification, as distinct from the balance shown in the records. In stores parlance, the quantity so found is referred to as the:
e: The quantity actually found on physical verification is the ground balance, as distinct from the book or ledger balance shown in the records and the bin balance.

q: The AAC of an item is 10,800 units. Coverage for five months is required to be provided. The stock in hand is 1,150 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 550 units. The quantity to be ordered is:
e: Requirement for 5 months = (10,800 / 12) x 5 = 900 x 5 = 4,500 units. Quantity to order = 4,500 - stock 1,150 - dues 550 = 2,800 units.

q: In the terminology of the General Financial Rules, the Security Deposit taken from a successful tenderer to secure the due performance of a stores contract is referred to as:
e: In GFR terminology, the Security Deposit taken from the successful tenderer to secure due performance of the contract is called Performance Security, while the tender-stage deposit is Bid Security.

q: The re-order level of an item is 2,100 units. The average consumption is 125 units per week and the average lead time is 9 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum stock level = re-order level - (average consumption x average lead time) = 2,100 - (125 x 9) = 2,100 - 1,125 = 975 units.

q: A depot works out the cost incurred by it in inviting tenders for an item, inspecting the supplies and progressing its purchase orders. In inventory costing, this cost is classified as:
e: Costs of inviting tenders, inspection and progressing purchase orders are costs of placing and following up orders, classified in inventory costing as ordering cost, distinct from carrying cost and purchase price.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 4,75,000. The advance payment admissible at 98% of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment = 98 per cent of Rs 4,75,000 = 4,75,000 x 0.98 = Rs 4,65,500, admissible against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, the balance being paid on receipt and acceptance.

q: An officer carrying out an ABC analysis of the stores items of a depot first arranges all the items in:

options.A: Ascending order of their unit price
options.B: Descending order of their annual consumption value
options.C: Alphabetical order of their PL numbers
options.D: Descending order of their unit price

e: ABC analysis begins by ranking all items in descending order of annual consumption value (annual consumption x unit rate), so high-value items needing close control are identified first.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,800 units and the re-order quantity is 1,100 units. The minimum consumption is 70 units per week and the minimum lead time is 4 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum stock level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1,800 + 1,100 - (70 x 4) = 2,900 - 280 = 2,620 units.

q: A depot holds large numbers of 'C' category fasteners and similar low-value items consumed in bulk. Such items are controlled loosely in that they are:

options.A: Verified by stock verifiers every month
options.B: Stocked with no buffer stock at all
options.C: Procured only against a Proprietary Article Certificate
options.D: Purchased in bulk for longer periods, with simple records and control

e: Low-value C category items consumed in bulk, like fasteners, are controlled loosely: purchased in bulk for longer periods with simple records and control, unlike the close control over A items.

q: A supplier fails to supply 550 units of stores contracted at Rs 70 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 88 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost of risk purchase = quantity x (risk purchase rate - contract rate) = 550 x (Rs 88 - Rs 70) = 550 x 18 = Rs 9,900, recoverable from the defaulting supplier under the risk purchase clause.

q: An item is deleted from the Priced Vocabulary of a railway and a stores officer proposes to allot the same PL number at once to a newly introduced item. The correct position is that the deleted item's PL number is:

options.A: Immediately allotted to the newly introduced item
options.B: Not re-allotted to any other item, so that the past records of the item remain unambiguous
options.C: Transferred to the list of non-stock items
options.D: Allotted to the depot's imprest stores

e: A deleted item's PL number is not re-allotted to any other item, so that past transactions and records under that number remain unambiguous for accounts and verification.

q: Wagons carrying a stores consignment to a depot are detained beyond the free time allowed for unloading them, and a charge becomes payable for the detention. As distinct from ground rent, this charge is payable as:

options.A: Storage charges for rejected material kept in the depot
options.B: Ground rent for scrap kept beyond the delivery period
options.D: Departmental charges on the stores received

e: The charge for wagons detained beyond the free time allowed for unloading is demurrage. Ground rent, by contrast, applies to scrap or material kept in the depot beyond the delivery period.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 190 units per week, its normal consumption is 140 units per week and the lead time is 5 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided for the item is:
e: Safety stock = (maximum consumption - normal consumption) x lead time = (190 - 140) x 5 = 50 x 5 = 250 units, covering consumption above normal during the lead time.

q: A depot adopts the periodic review system for a stock item, under which its stock position is examined at fixed intervals. Under this system, an order is placed at each review:

options.A: To restore the stock to a predetermined target level
options.B: For a fixed quantity, whenever the stock falls to the re-order level
options.C: Only when the stock is completely exhausted
options.D: By the supplier automatically, without a review by the depot

e: Under the periodic review system the stock position is reviewed at fixed intervals and an order is placed at each review to restore the stock to a predetermined target level.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 38 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 225 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:
e: Value of shortage = shortage quantity x book rate = 38 x Rs 225 = Rs 8,550, which is accounted for through the stock sheet and Stock Adjustment Account pending recovery or write-off.

q: A zonal railway procures a new item of equipment, for which costly spares will be needed as insurance against a prolonged breakdown. Such insurance (capital) spares for the equipment are ordinarily procured:

options.A: Only after the equipment is commissioned
options.B: Only when the equipment first breaks down
options.C: Along with the procurement of the main equipment itself
options.D: From the scrap released from similar equipment

e: Costly insurance or capital spares for new equipment are procured along with the main equipment itself, so they are available whenever a breakdown occurs and are not awaited after commissioning.

q: Stores are issued from a depot to a contractor for use on a railway work being executed by him. The value of such stores is dealt with by:

options.A: Making no charge, as the stores belong to the Railway
options.B: Recovering the value in cash from the contractor before the issue
options.C: Writing off the value to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: Debiting the value, at the rates prescribed in the contract, to the work and recovering it from the amounts payable to the contractor

e: Stores issued to a contractor for a railway work are debited to the work at the rates prescribed in the contract and their value recovered from the amounts payable to the contractor; they are never a free issue.

q: The average consumption of an item is 70 units per day and the lead time for emergency procurement is 7 days. The danger level of the item is:
e: Danger level = average consumption per day x lead time for emergency procurement = 70 x 7 = 490 units, the level at which emergency procurement action must be initiated.

q: A Permanent Way depot requires rails, sleepers and track fittings for maintenance and renewal of track. Such track materials are stocked in depots known as:

options.D: Imprest stores held by field officials

e: Rails, sleepers and track fittings for maintenance and renewal of track are stocked in P-Way (Permanent Way) stores depots, the specialised depots for track materials.

q: A supplier offers a quantity discount if a depot orders an item in a much larger quantity than its Economic Order Quantity. The decision whether to avail of the discount is taken by:

options.A: Always accepting the largest quantity, as the unit price is the lowest
options.B: Comparing only the ordering costs at each quantity
options.C: Comparing the total cost — purchase cost, ordering cost and carrying cost — at the Economic Order Quantity and at each price-break quantity
options.D: Comparing only the carrying costs at each quantity

e: A quantity discount offer is judged by comparing the total cost - purchase cost plus ordering cost plus carrying cost - at the EOQ and at each price-break quantity, not by unit price alone.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 1.35 crore. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 15 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:
e: Annual inventory carrying cost = 15 per cent of average stock value = 0.15 x Rs 1,35,00,000 = Rs 20,25,000 per annum.

q: A supplier claims interest for the period for which his Earnest Money Deposit and Security Deposit remained with the Railways under a stores contract. The correct position is that:

options.A: No interest is payable by the Railways on either amount
options.B: Interest is payable on both amounts at the bank rate
options.C: Interest is payable only on the Security Deposit
options.D: Interest is payable only if the supplies were completed before time

e: No interest is payable by the Railways on Earnest Money Deposit or Security Deposit held under a stores contract, whatever the period for which the amounts remain deposited.

q: For administrative convenience, the purchase work at a zonal railway headquarters is divided into groups, each group dealing with a set of allied items. Each such purchase group functions under the charge of:
e: At zonal headquarters, purchase work is organised in groups of allied items, and each purchase group functions under a Chief Materials Manager, the group officer for that set of items.

q: A depot holds 1,250 units of an item. The book rate of the item is revised from Rs 48 to Rs 54 per unit. The increase in the value of the stock in hand, which is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: Increase in stock value = quantity in hand x increase in book rate = 1,250 x (Rs 54 - Rs 48) = 1,250 x 6 = Rs 7,500, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: A firm pays the prescribed price for the tender documents of a stores tender but does not submit a tender, and claims refund of the price paid. The correct position is that the price charged for the tender documents is:

options.A: Refunded to the firm, as it submitted no tender
options.B: Adjusted against the earnest money deposit of the firm
options.C: Refunded if the tender is discharged without acceptance
options.D: Not refundable, whether or not the firm submits a tender

e: The price charged for tender documents is the cost of the documents and is not refundable, whether or not the firm that bought them submits a tender.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 9 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 28 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 31 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:

options.A: A debit balance of Rs 6 lakh
options.B: A debit balance of Rs 4 lakh
options.C: A debit balance of Rs 5 lakh
options.D: A debit balance of Rs 7 lakh

e: Closing Purchase Suspense = opening debit Rs 9 lakh + bills paid Rs 28 lakh - material received and linked Rs 31 lakh = a debit balance of Rs 6 lakh, representing payments awaiting linkage with receipts.

q: In ABC analysis, the 'B' category items of a depot are subjected to:

options.A: The same close control as 'A' category items
options.B: Moderate control — less close than that exercised over 'A' category items but closer than that over 'C' category items
options.C: No control at all, as they are insignificant in value
options.D: Control only at the time of the annual stock verification

e: In ABC analysis, B category items get moderate control - less close than A items, which carry the highest consumption value, but closer than the loose control over low-value C items.

q: The equipment using a stock item has been withdrawn from service and, on review, the item is no longer required to be stocked. The item is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Continuing it in the Priced Vocabulary for ever, without any change
options.B: Transferring it compulsorily to every other depot
options.C: Deleting it from the stock list/Priced Vocabulary, the balance stock held, if any, being dealt with as surplus
options.D: Issuing the balance stock free of cost to the depot staff

e: An item no longer required because its equipment is withdrawn is deleted from the stock list or Priced Vocabulary, and any balance stock held is dealt with as surplus stores.

q: A stores depot issues 400 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 90 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 12.5 per cent of the book value. The total amount recoverable from the party is:
e: Book value of issue = 400 x Rs 90 = Rs 36,000. Departmental charges at 12.5 per cent = Rs 4,500. Total recoverable = 36,000 + 4,500 = Rs 40,500.

q: In the replenishment cycle of a stock item, the stock which is regularly consumed and replenished between two successive receipts of the item is known as its:

options.B: Stock held in excess of the maximum level
options.C: Stock reserved only for meeting emergencies
options.D: Stock awaiting inspection and acceptance at the depot

e: Cycle stock is the stock regularly consumed and replenished between two successive receipts in the replenishment cycle, as distinct from safety stock held against fluctuations.

q: While prescribing coverage for stock items, Headquarters prescribes a lower coverage, in months, for high-value 'A' category items than for low-value 'C' category items, mainly in order to:

options.A: Increase the stock of 'A' category items held in depots
options.B: Limit the capital locked up in high-value stock
options.C: Ensure that 'A' category items are purchased more frequently at higher rates
options.D: Reduce the number of purchase orders placed for 'C' category items

e: Lower coverage in months for high-value A items limits the capital locked up in such stock, while low-value C items can safely carry longer coverage without blocking much capital.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 8,100 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 50 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit per year. When orders are placed in Economic Order Quantities, the total of the annual ordering cost and the annual carrying cost is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x 8,100 x 50 / 4) = square root of 2,02,500 = 450 units. Ordering cost = (8,100 / 450) x 50 = Rs 900 and carrying cost = (450 / 2) x 4 = Rs 900, so the total is Rs 1,800.

q: The Turnover Ratio of the stores of a railway is 0.16 and the closing balance of stores is Rs 80 lakh. The total issues of stores during the year are:
e: Total issues = closing balance / Turnover Ratio = Rs 80 lakh / 0.16 = Rs 500 lakh = Rs 5 crore, using the ratio as closing stock relative to issues.

q: Four wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 5 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading. Demurrage is payable at Rs 900 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Total demurrage = wagons x days x rate per wagon per day = 4 x 5 x Rs 900 = Rs 18,000 for detention beyond the free unloading time.

q: For certain common items of stores, rate contracts are concluded centrally by the Railway Board. A zonal railway which requires such an item obtains its supplies by:

options.A: Inviting fresh tenders for every requirement
options.B: Placing supply orders on the firm against the Railway Board's rate contract
options.C: Purchasing the item from the open market at market rates
options.D: Manufacturing the item in railway workshops only

e: For items covered by a Railway Board rate contract, a zonal railway obtains supplies by placing supply orders directly on the contracted firm against that rate contract, without inviting fresh tenders.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 84 lakh and the closing balance is Rs 56 lakh. The average stock held during the year is:
e: Average stock = (opening balance + closing balance) / 2 = (Rs 84 lakh + Rs 56 lakh) / 2 = Rs 140 lakh / 2 = Rs 70 lakh.

q: A depot needs a petty stores item of small value urgently. The requirement is met by a local (spot) purchase. In such a purchase:

options.A: The storekeeper alone purchases the item from any shop without keeping any record
options.B: Tenders are invited through advertisement in the press
options.C: A Spot Purchase Committee inspects the material available in the market and purchases it on the spot at a reasonable rate
options.D: The material is borrowed permanently from another depot

e: An urgent petty local purchase is made through a Spot Purchase Committee, which inspects the material available in the market and purchases it on the spot at a reasonable rate; it is not a lone storekeeper purchase.

q: A newly posted stores officer wants to refer to the priced list of stores items which shows the PL number, the nomenclature (description and unit) and the book rate of each item. The list he should consult is the:

options.B: Rate Contract list of the railway

e: The priced list showing each item's PL number, nomenclature with unit, and book rate is the Priced Vocabulary of stores, the master priced list of all stocked items.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 52 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 1.84 crore and issues during the year are Rs 1.66 crore. The closing balance of stores is:
e: Closing balance = opening balance + receipts - issues = Rs 52 lakh + Rs 184 lakh - Rs 166 lakh = Rs 70 lakh.

q: In the programme of periodical stock verification of a stores depot, the high-value 'A' category items are verified:

options.D: Only when the custodian of the depot changes

e: In the periodical stock verification programme under the Stores Code, high-value A category items are verified twice a year, more frequently than B and C items, because of the capital locked up in them.

q: Apart from the programmed periodical verification of stores, the stock verifiers of the Accounts Department may also carry out:

options.A: Verification only when the custodian himself requests it
options.B: Verification of the personal accounts of the depot staff
options.C: Surprise checks of stores balances, without prior intimation to the custodian
options.D: Physical verification of works under execution

e: Besides programmed periodical verification, Accounts stock verifiers may carry out surprise checks of stores balances without prior intimation to the custodian, so balances are tested as actually maintained.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 96 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 2.44 crore and the closing balance is Rs 80 lakh. The total issues of stores during the year are:
e: Total issues = opening balance + receipts - closing balance = Rs 96 lakh + Rs 244 lakh - Rs 80 lakh = Rs 260 lakh = Rs 2.60 crore.

q: Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, the annual procurement target from MSEs is 25 per cent. Within this target, the sub-target for MSEs owned by Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs is:
e: Under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs, the annual target is 25 per cent of procurement from MSEs, within which the sub-target for MSEs owned by SC/ST entrepreneurs is 4 per cent.

q: A micro enterprise demands payment for its supplies within 60 days of acceptance, as provided in its agreement with the Railway. Under the MSMED Act, the agreed date for payment cannot in any case exceed:

options.A: 30 days from the date of acceptance of the supplies
options.B: 90 days from the date of acceptance of the supplies
options.C: 45 days from the date of acceptance of the supplies
options.D: 15 days from the date of acceptance of the supplies

e: Under the MSMED Act, the date agreed for payment to a micro or small enterprise cannot exceed 45 days from the date of acceptance or deemed acceptance of the supplies, so a 60-day term is not permissible.

q: The minimum level of a stock item is 550 units and its maximum level is 2,150 units. The average stock level of the item is:
e: Average stock level = (minimum level + maximum level) / 2 = (550 + 2,150) / 2 = 2,700 / 2 = 1,350 units.

q: A reverse auction is conducted on IREPS for the purchase of stores among the tenderers whose offers have been found technically acceptable. In the reverse auction:

options.A: Bidders compete by quoting successively higher prices
options.B: Only the highest bidder is considered for award of the contract
options.C: Bidding starts from the highest price received in the tender
options.D: Bidding starts from the lowest price received in the tender and bidders compete by quoting successively lower prices

e: In a reverse auction on IREPS among technically acceptable tenderers, bidding starts from the lowest price received in the tender and bidders compete by quoting successively lower prices.

q: A lot of scrap is sold by e-auction and the purchaser asks whether the taxes and duties leviable on the sale are included in his bid price. The correct position is that such taxes and duties are payable:

options.A: By the Railway out of the bid price realised
options.B: By the purchaser, in addition to the bid price
options.C: By the stores depot conducting the auction
options.D: Equally by the Railway and the purchaser

e: In scrap e-auction sales, taxes and duties leviable on the sale are payable by the purchaser in addition to his bid price, not borne by the Railway out of the price realised.

q: A depot holds 2,650 units of an item, whereas the maximum level fixed for the item is 2,200 units. The book rate of the item is Rs 44 per unit. The value of the stock held in excess of the maximum level is:
e: Stock in excess of maximum = 2,650 - 2,200 = 450 units. Value of excess = 450 x Rs 44 = Rs 19,800, showing the capital blocked in overstocking.

q: An enquiry into the conduct of a supplier firm is in progress and, pending its completion, business dealings with the firm are held in abeyance. Such suspension of business dealings, as distinct from banning of the firm, is:

options.A: An interim measure adopted pending completion of the enquiry into the conduct of the firm
options.B: A permanent measure taken after a full enquiry
options.C: A measure applicable only to foreign firms
options.D: A measure which can be taken only after the firm has first been banned

e: Suspension of business dealings is an interim measure adopted pending completion of the enquiry into a firm's conduct, distinct from banning, which is a final measure taken after the enquiry.

q: A Stores Tender Committee consists of the Stores Officer and the Finance member. Besides these two, the committee also includes:

options.A: A representative of the lowest tenderer
options.B: The depot storekeeper of the consignee depot
options.C: A nominee of the Railway Board in every case
options.D: A representative of the indenting (user) department, for technical evaluation of the offers

e: A Stores Tender Committee comprises the Stores Officer, the Finance member and a representative of the indenting or user department, who provides the technical evaluation of the offers.

q: During stock verification, 22 units of an item are found in excess of the book balance. The book rate of the item is Rs 260 per unit. The value of the excess taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account is:
e: Value of excess = excess quantity x book rate = 22 x Rs 260 = Rs 5,720, taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account on the stock sheet.

q: In one system of inventory accounting, the stock in hand is ascertained only by a physical count made at intervals, and book balances are not maintained continuously after every receipt and issue. That system is the:
e: In the periodic system of inventory, stock in hand is ascertained only by physical count at intervals and no continuous book balance is maintained after every receipt and issue, unlike the perpetual inventory system.

q: A stores depot receives an item manufactured in a railway workshop and transferred to it for stocking, and prepares a Receipt Note for taking the item into stock. A Receipt Note is likewise prepared for stores received from:

options.A: All sources — purchases, workshop manufacture, transfers from other depots and returns from departments/works

e: A Receipt Note is prepared for stores received from all sources - outside purchases, workshop manufacture, transfers from other depots and returns from departments or works - to bring the receipt into priced stock.

q: The average consumption of an item is 135 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 7 weeks. The consumption of the item during the lead time is:
e: Consumption during lead time = average consumption x lead time = 135 x 7 = 945 units, the quantity expected to be consumed while a replenishment order is executed.

q: A supplier participating in a stores tender under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order declares a local content of 15 per cent in the item offered. The supplier is treated as:
e: Under the Make in India Order, a supplier with local content below 20 per cent (here 15 per cent) is a non-local supplier; Class-II needs 20 to 50 per cent and Class-I needs 50 per cent or more.

q: A specialised item of equipment is not manufactured in the country at all. Such specialised stores and equipment may be procured through:

options.C: A single tender placed by the depot officer
options.D: Purchase against the imprest of the depot

e: Specialised stores and equipment not manufactured in the country are procured through global tenders invited internationally, so capable foreign manufacturers can compete for the requirement.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 7,200 units and its Economic Order Quantity is 600 units. If the cost of placing one order is Rs 275, the total ordering cost per year is:
e: Number of orders per year = annual requirement / EOQ = 7,200 / 600 = 12. Total ordering cost = 12 x Rs 275 = Rs 3,300 per year.

q: After the model SOP of 2018, vetting of AAC by Headquarters Finance is confined to 'A' category items. The AAC of 'B' and 'C' category items is accordingly fixed:

options.A: By the Railway Board in every case
options.B: By the supplier of the item
options.C: By the Inspector of Stores Accounts
options.D: At the zonal/divisional (depot) level, without vetting by Headquarters Finance

e: After the model SOP of 2018, Headquarters Finance vetting of AAC is confined to A category items. AAC of B and C items is fixed at the zonal or divisional (depot) level without that vetting.

q: Goods ordered on the Government e-Marketplace are received and accepted by the consignee, who generates the Consignee's Receipt and Acceptance Certificate (CRAC). Payment to the seller is thereafter required to be made within:
e: On GeM, once the consignee generates the Consignee's Receipt and Acceptance Certificate (CRAC) after receipt and acceptance, payment to the seller must be made within 10 days.

q: The book rate of an item is Rs 340 per unit and the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 15 per cent per annum of the stock value. The carrying cost per unit per year is:
e: Carrying cost per unit per year = book rate x carrying cost rate = Rs 340 x 15 per cent = Rs 51 per unit per year.

q: An item is transferred from one depot of a railway to another depot of the same railway, where the same item is already stocked. In the priced accounts of the receiving depot, the item is accounted for under:

options.A: A new PL number allotted by the receiving depot for the transferred stock
options.B: The same PL number which the item bears in every depot where it is stocked
options.C: The PL number of a similar item already held by the depot
options.D: A temporary PL number used only for transferred stores

e: An item bears one PL number wherever it is stocked. A transferred item is therefore accounted in the receiving depot under the same PL number, not a new or temporary number.

q: The AAC of a stock item is revised upward from 6,000 units to 7,200 units, while the stock in hand and the dues remain unchanged. The coverage of the item, expressed in months, will:

options.C: Increase in the same proportion as the AAC

e: Coverage in months equals stock plus dues divided by monthly consumption derived from AAC. If AAC rises while stock and dues stay unchanged, monthly consumption rises and the coverage in months decreases.

q: The safety (buffer) stock of an item is 275 units and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 14 per unit per year. The annual carrying cost attributable to the safety stock is:
e: Annual carrying cost of safety stock = safety stock x carrying cost per unit = 275 x Rs 14 = Rs 3,850 per year, the cost of holding the buffer.

q: In a periodical review of the 'dues' of a depot — the quantities of stores already on order with suppliers — the review is undertaken mainly to:

options.A: Increase the closing balance of stores of the depot
options.B: Fix the book rate of the items on order
options.C: Cancel or short-close orders for items which are no longer required, and thereby avoid excess procurement
options.D: Prepare the catalogue for the next e-auction of scrap

e: Periodical review of dues (quantities already on order) is mainly to cancel or short-close orders for items no longer required, preventing excess procurement and blocking of funds.

q: Oils and paints, which are consumed in use, are issued from a depot to a consuming department. Such consumable stores, once issued, are:

options.A: Required to be returned to the depot after use
options.B: Finally charged off to the consuming head at the time of issue itself, no return being required
options.C: Borne on the Tools and Plant register of the department
options.D: Physically verified in the department every year

e: Consumable stores like oils and paints are finally charged off to the consuming head at the time of issue itself. Being consumed in use, they are not returned to the depot or carried on a Tools and Plant register.

q: An item has an Economic Order Quantity of 950 units and a safety stock of 225 units. Under the EOQ system with a uniform rate of consumption, the average inventory of the item held is:
e: Average inventory under EOQ with uniform consumption = EOQ / 2 + safety stock = 950 / 2 + 225 = 475 + 225 = 700 units.

q: A Stores Accounts clerk is listing the suspense and adjustment heads operated in the Stores Accounts of a railway. Which one of the following does NOT belong to that list?
e: Purchase Suspense, Sales Suspense and Stores Miscellaneous Suspense are Stores Accounts heads. Workshop Manufacturing Suspense belongs to workshop accounts, not to the list of Stores Accounts suspense and adjustment heads.

q: Unserviceable stores in a depot are to be examined for condemnation and disposal. The survey committee appointed for the purpose ordinarily consists of representatives of:

options.B: The supplier firms which had supplied the stores
options.C: The Stores Department, the user department and the Accounts/Finance Department
options.D: The Railway Protection Force and the user department

e: A survey committee for condemnation and disposal of unserviceable stores ordinarily has representatives of the Stores Department, the user department and the Accounts or Finance Department, so technical, user and financial views are all present.

q: A purchase order is placed on a supplier for stores valued at Rs 8,40,000. The security deposit prescribed under the contract at 5 per cent of the order value works out to:
e: Security Deposit = 5 per cent of order value = 0.05 x Rs 8,40,000 = Rs 42,000, furnished as Performance Security for due fulfilment of the contract.

q: Through the UDM of iMMS, a consuming department can view the stock position of items in depots and raise its demands online. In iMMS, 'UDM' stands for:
e: In iMMS, UDM stands for User Depot Module, through which a consuming department (user depot) views stock positions in depots and raises its demands online.

q: A depot lists four ways of getting rid of its surplus and unserviceable stores. Which one of the following is NOT a recognised mode of disposal of such stores on the Railways?

options.A: Return to the original supplier as a matter of course at the purchase price
options.B: Transfer to another depot or railway requiring the stores

e: Surplus and unserviceable stores are disposed of by transfer to another depot or railway, sale to other Government departments, or sale through e-auction. Return to the original supplier at the purchase price as a matter of course is not a recognised mode.

q: A stores depot issues 675 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 56 per unit. The value of the issue debited to the consuming department is:
e: Value of issue = quantity issued x book rate = 675 x Rs 56 = Rs 37,800, debited to the consuming department at the average book rate.

q: A firm seeks approval of RDSO as a vendor for the supply of a safety (critical) stores item. Before such approval is granted, the firm is required to obtain approval of its:
e: Vendor approval by RDSO for a safety or critical item requires prior approval of the firm's Quality Assurance Programme (QAP), so its quality system is verified before it is approved as a vendor.

q: Issues of stores from railway depots are priced at the average (book) rate of the item. Which of the following methods is NOT followed on the Railways?

options.A: Weighted average (book) rate for pricing issues
options.B: First In, First Out (FIFO) for physical issue of stores
options.C: Uniform issue rate at all depots of the railway

e: Issues on the Railways are priced at the weighted average book rate and physical issue broadly follows FIFO, with a uniform issue rate at all depots of the railway. LIFO is not followed.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 3,850 units and its book rate is Rs 190 per unit. For the purposes of ABC analysis, the annual consumption value of the item is:
e: Annual consumption value for ABC analysis = annual consumption x book rate = 3,850 x Rs 190 = Rs 7,31,500, the basis for ranking the item in the ABC order.

q: A tenderer has submitted his bid for stores on IREPS and, before the due date and time fixed for submission of tenders, wishes to modify it. The tenderer may modify or withdraw the bid:

options.A: At any time before the opening of the tenders, even after the due date
options.B: Only within one hour of submitting the bid
options.C: At any time before the due date and time fixed for submission of tenders
options.D: Not at all, once the bid has been submitted

e: On IREPS, a tenderer may modify or withdraw his bid at any time before the due date and time fixed for submission of tenders; after that time the bid cannot be changed.

q: An outside party to whom stores are issued questions the departmental charges levied in addition to the book value, treating them as a profit margin of the Railways. In fact, the departmental charges represent, broadly:

options.A: The freight payable for despatch of the stores to the party
options.B: The cost incurred by the Railways on handling, storage, supervision and accounting of the stores
options.C: The customs duty paid by the Railways on the stores
options.D: A profit margin earned by the Railways on the issue of the stores

e: Departmental charges levied over book value on issues to outside parties represent broadly the Railway's cost of handling, storage, supervision and accounting of the stores, not a profit margin.

q: Scrap having a book value of Rs 46,000 is sold by e-auction for Rs 61,500. The excess of the sale value over the book value, amounting to Rs 15,500, is:

options.A: Debited to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.B: Credited to the Purchase Suspense Account
options.C: Adjusted against the security deposit of the purchaser
options.D: Credited to the Stock Adjustment Account

e: Scrap is sold above book value: Rs 61,500 - Rs 46,000 = Rs 15,500 excess. The excess of sale value over book value realised on disposal of stores is credited to the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: A supplier has defaulted in supplying a part of the quantity ordered on him and the Railway decides to effect a risk purchase for the quantity in default. Before the risk purchase is effected, the original purchase order is, in respect of that quantity:

options.A: Cancelled (short-closed) for the defaulted quantity, after giving due notice to the supplier
options.B: Kept open indefinitely till the supplier chooses to supply

e: Before a risk purchase is made for a defaulted quantity, the original purchase order is cancelled or short-closed for that quantity after due notice to the supplier, so the risk purchase is made at his risk and cost under GCC for Supply.
